Aviation history is getting its doors back open. ✈️💛

Oregon’s Tillamook Air Museum plans to reopen October 29 at 10 a.m., nearly ten months after a storm damaged its historic World War II-era Hangar B.

The comeback has a community behind it. Nearly 80 volunteers gathered October 9 to move airplanes, clean exhibits and prepare the museum for visitors. Friends of the Tillamook Air Museum also contributed $50,000 toward repairs to the storm-damaged roof.

The museum now has a new nonprofit owner and operator, Vintage Aviation Museum. Tillamook staff remain on site caring for the hangar, aircraft and collection.

The reopening is a milestone, with preservation work still ahead. The friends group says the $50,000 is a start—not the full cost of protecting the building.

For aviation fans, it means another chance to explore the collection inside a remarkable survivor of the blimp era—and see what a community can help keep alive.

Planning a visit? Check the museum’s website for the latest reopening details and hours.
